items.excerpt: At PGC Summit Shanghai, studio leaders and investors asked why free-to-play mobile races to adopt AI in production while triple-A holds back. The panel maps where AI is actually landing in game pipelines and where it stalls.

Ludo.ai has launched Keyframe Animation, a tool giving game developers direct control over AI-generated sprite animations, alongside new 3D asset tooling. It pushes generative art from one-shot output toward editable, art-directable frames.

A gamescom dev speaker survey found AI-assisted development is expected to have the biggest impact on the games industry over the next three years, paired with a shift to smaller teams. Respondents point to changing role definitions rather than pure headcount cuts.

Meta introduced Meta XR Operator, an experimental tool that lets AI coding agents autonomously build, test, debug and visually verify VR apps. It aims the agent loop at the hardest part of XR production: actually playing the build and checking what it looks like.

A withering look at Google's latest AI-made game showcase: '...we are 3-4 years into this collective descent into madness, and this is all you can come up with to support [AI's] sales pitch?' A critique of what generative demos still can't do as playable design.

Kotaku catalogues the gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 lineup by generative-AI usage, noting several titles newly outed as using genAI art or voice. A snapshot of how AI disclosure has become a front-of-show reception filter.

A hands-on with Sega's Crazy Taxi: World Tour that keeps circling back to the game's Steam generative-AI disclosure. The preview shows how an AI disclaimer now colours the whole critical read of a revival.

Atelier has turned Ryza into RyzaChat: AI, an open-ended chatbot companion app on iOS and Android in Japan. The team frames it as an 'ethical AI adventure' — no chat logs used for training, and a voice trained only on the original Japanese actor's clips.

As anti-AI clauses start appearing in publishing and dev contracts, GamesRadar argues player backlash is materially changing what studios are allowed to ship. A look at how audience pressure is rewriting production policy.

Dragon Quest creator Yuji Horii says AI 'hardly ever makes things up' anymore and defends building the conversational companion Slimey into the series, arguing it 'lowers the barrier of entry to interacting with AI.'

Take-Two's former head of AI turns skeptic, arguing LLM dialogue hasn't landed because '50 or 100 options' in a dialogue tree mostly lead nowhere. A pointed design critique of generative narrative from someone who built for it.

PC Gamer's Steam week-in-review tracks how even a small amount of generative AI in an indie's assets now triggers review-bomb-scale backlash. Useful data on where the audience's disclosure tolerance actually sits.
An argument against the executive push for AI-generated NPCs and writing, framing infinite generated dialogue as a substitute for authored craft rather than an upgrade to it.

Sega rewrote Crazy Taxi: World Tour's Steam AI disclosure to say generative AI was used only for ideation on background objects — and that all AI-derived content will be removed before release. A concrete case of disclosure language becoming a production commitment.

Dark and Darker studio IRONMACE describes how AI coding assistant Aura let a non-technical designer work directly in the codebase to prototype and ship the game's new tutorial — a job the studio estimates would normally have taken five to six weeks, done in two.

A full recap of the Rideshare 'Stimulator' dispute: a lead writer says she was replaced mid-project by ChatGPT, the CEO apologises, and Saber finally adds a Steam AI disclosure covering voice generation, localisation and radio music.

Saber Interactive's CEO apologises to a former employee over the AI replacement dispute while denying writers were swapped for ChatGPT. The piece lays out what parts of the shipped game are AI-generated and what disclosure was owed.

Saber CEO Matt Karch says a Portal writer's viral video triggered death threats, escalating the Rideshare Stimulator AI-writer dispute. The updated Steam page now specifies AI voice generation, some localisation and AI radio music.

A weekly roundup of CG tool updates relevant to game art: Meshy 7's higher-fidelity image-to-3D generation, Postshot 1.1.69 for Gaussian splats, and Slapshot's rotoscoping, camera-tracking and depth-map tools shipping as nodes inside Comfy.
